You are the reviewer agent in a five-role engineering team.

SPECIFICATION:
Build a small Python 3 standard-library-only order processing system. It must work across multiple module boundaries and JSON snapshot/restore. Produce ledger.py, outbox.py, service.py, and HANDOFF.md. No network, filesystem writes, subprocesses, or external packages in candidate code. Deterministic caller-supplied time; no wall-clock calls.

ledger.py: Ledger(snapshot=None). apply(event) -> bool. event is exactly a dictionary with nonempty string id, order_id, kind and a positive integer amount (booleans are invalid). kind is reserve, capture, or refund. A reserve creates a new order and sets its reserved amount; a second reserve for the same order is invalid. Capture requires an existing order and cumulative capture <= reserved. Refund requires cumulative refund <= captured. All invalid events raise ValueError and change neither balances nor deduplication state. Reusing an event id with identical content returns False; reusing it with different content raises ValueError. An accepted new event returns True. balances(order_id) returns {reserved, captured, refunded, available, net}, with available=reserved-captured and net=captured-refunded; unknown order raises KeyError. snapshot() returns a JSON-serializable value. Constructor and snapshot must deep-copy their input/output.

outbox.py: Outbox(snapshot=None). enqueue(key, payload) -> bool: new nonempty string key returns True; same key and equal JSON payload returns False; same key different payload raises ValueError. Copy payloads, do not alias callers. claim(worker, now, lease) -> None or {key,payload,version}; worker must be a nonempty string and lease > 0, invalid inputs raise ValueError. Select the earliest-enqueued uncompleted item whose lease is absent or expired (now >= expiry). Each claim/reclaim increments that item's version. A completed item is never reissued. complete(key, worker, version, now) -> bool: only the current, unexpired owner with exact version may complete; all unknown/stale/wrong owner/already completed attempts return False without changes. snapshot() and constructor use JSON-serializable deep copies.

service.py: Service(snapshot=None) exposes ledger and outbox attributes, ingest(event) -> bool, dispatch(worker,now,lease,sink) -> bool, snapshot(). ingest applies one event and enqueues a notification with key event['id'] and payload equal to event. Duplicate events must not enqueue twice. If enqueue raises, roll back both ledger and outbox and re-raise. dispatch claims one item, calls sink(key,payload), then completes with exact owner/version at supplied now. No available item returns False; successful delivery and completion returns True. If sink raises, propagate and leave the lease outstanding. On expiry a retry is allowed. A process can die after the sink applies an effect but before completion: sink must implement durable idempotency by key; never promise exactly-once transport. Service.snapshot() covers both components. Restoration and snapshots must not alias live state.

HANDOFF.md: 120–220 words, for the engineer resuming this work. Explain module responsibilities, event-id idempotency, expiry/reclaim and stale-owner rejection, sink success-before-ack crash window, and the boundary of the in-memory transaction (a production database transaction is still needed). State limitations plainly. Do not claim the underlying queue alone gives exactly-once external effects. Do not invent test counts or performance claims.

All callers operate serially within one Service instance; thread-safe candidate internals are not required. Snapshot inputs are valid snapshots emitted by the matching class, possibly round-tripped through JSON. There are no hidden schema requirements for snapshot internals. Hidden tests exercise only the public behavior above. Return a JSON object with a files mapping from the requested names to their full contents. Additional prose outside JSON is tolerated by extraction, but files must parse and run.


YOUR STAGE:
Review and repair the complete implementation. Check all requirements, including aliasing, atomicity, and stale ownership. Return all four final files. Public smoke-test feedback (other checks remain hidden):
